job_description_info.job_description:
# Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI

**Company:** Quillstone Payments (fictional name; card-payment and business-tools provider)
**Location:** Hamburg, Germany (office-first)
**Team:** AI team within Customer Operations

## About the team

The Customer Operations organisation wants merchants to get help quickly and without friction. The AI team builds models and assistants that answer merchant questions, route tickets and help support agents. You will work with backend engineers, data scientists and product managers to take ideas from prototype to production.

## What you will do

- Build, deploy and operate AI and machine learning systems used by the support organisation
- Maintain pipelines for data processing, training and serving
- Fine-tune and evaluate models, including language models, for accuracy and cost
- Prepare and clean large text datasets
- Apply normal engineering discipline: version control, CI/CD and automated tests
- Integrate ML components into the wider product with other engineering teams

## Requirements

- Degree in machine learning, computer science or a related engineering field
- At least four years of experience as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production
- Experience with AI products such as chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
- Software engineering skills for production systems: model serving, monitoring, data versioning
- Experience with a major cloud provider (AWS, GCP or Azure)
- Strong Python; familiarity with MLOps and orchestration tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow or an LLM-observability tool
- Experience with feature engineering and data ingestion pipelines

## Benefits

- Annual learning budget, employee share programme and company pension contribution
- Relocation support and subsidised meals
- Sabbatical after several years of service

company_info.company_description:
Quillstone Payments is a privately held financial-services company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Hamburg. It builds payment and money-management tools for small merchants, including card terminals, a point-of-sale app and a business account. The company serves millions of merchants across Europe and the Americas and has recently added a personal account for merchants’ customers.

Quillstone’s culture combines team autonomy with shared principles rather than heavy processes. Teams own their services and work across product, engineering and operations to solve merchants’ problems. The company values ownership, teamwork, pragmatism, humility, candid feedback and learning from mistakes, with open sharing of context encouraged. It describes itself as office-first, while allowing teams some flexible days, and supports development through training budgets, peer feedback, internal tech talks and twice-yearly development-plan reviews. Other notable features include a machine-learning group focused on customer-support automation and fraud models, relocation support for many roles, and support for local business education projects and inclusion reporting.

I am drawn to the opportunity to build AI systems that help merchants get support quickly and help support teams work more effectively.

In my current role at Slavonica Document AI, I developed and deployed a classifier for scanned public-administration documents that achieves 94% accuracy and a 0.91 macro F1 score across 23 classes, processing approximately 15,000 documents per day. I fine-tuned XLM-R and BERTić models for Croatian document classification and named entity recognition, and serve models through FastAPI and Docker on Azure. I also built production monitoring that helped identify an OCR change associated with a nine-percentage-point accuracy drop, which was resolved within a week. This work has given me hands-on experience taking ML systems from data preparation and experimentation through model serving, production monitoring and model versioning with MLflow.

My earlier work at Baranjska kreditna banka included classifying customer complaints into 11 topics to support weekly reporting for customer-service management. I have also built a weekend prototype for question answering over Croatian laws using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). This was a personal prototype, not a production system, and it strengthened my interest in language-based tools for finding and using relevant information. Across these projects, I have worked with Python, Azure, MLflow, PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers, and I value practical, evidence-led iteration.

Quillstone’s focus on customer-support automation and its emphasis on team ownership, open sharing of context and learning from mistakes appeal to me. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my production NLP, model-serving and monitoring experience and a pragmatic approach to the AI team and contribute to systems that make support more useful for merchants and agents.

Kind regards,
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional and well-targeted cover letter. It clearly identifies the role, presents relevant production NLP experience, uses quantified outcomes, and accurately distinguishes the RAG work as a personal prototype rather than production experience. The progression from document classification to customer complaint classification and RAG creates a credible connection to customer-support AI. The letter is concise and readable, with an appropriate professional tone. Its main limitation is that the final paragraphs could connect the candidate's experience more directly to Quillstone's support-assistant and ticket-routing use cases rather than relying mainly on general enthusiasm.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses ATS-friendly plain text, standard paragraphs, recognizable job-related terminology, and no problematic formatting, tables, graphics or unusual section structures. It includes strong keywords such as machine learning, NLP, production ML systems, Python, Azure, FastAPI, Docker, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, MLflow, model serving, monitoring and RAG. AI screening probability is high for the requirements supported by the candidate's background. The letter does not explicitly include terms such as data ingestion pipelines, feature engineering, data versioning, CI/CD, automated tests or orchestration; however, the candidate information does not substantiate these capabilities, so they should not be added merely for keyword matching.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very well with the degree requirement, production ML experience, Azure, Python, MLOps, model serving, monitoring and RAG requirements. It also demonstrates relevant customer-support text classification through the 11-topic complaint-classification project. The candidate's document AI and NLP background is highly transferable to support ticket routing, merchant-question answering and agent-assistance systems. The letter appropriately presents the RAG project as a prototype and does not overstate LLM production experience. Material gaps are the literal requirement of at least four years specifically as a machine learning engineer shipping systems to production, since the documented ML Engineer role begins in 2023, and the lack of evidence for feature engineering, data ingestion pipelines and data versioning. These are candidate-background gaps rather than cover-letter defects. The letter references Quillstone's ownership, open context-sharing and learning-from-mistakes culture accurately, although the connection could be slightly more concrete.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the third paragraph, make the customer-support transfer more explicit by changing the sentence beginning "My earlier work at Baranjska kreditna banka" to explain that the 11-topic customer complaint classifier is directly relevant to support-ticket routing, triage or reporting. For example: "At Baranjska kreditna banka, I built an 11-topic customer-complaint classifier that supported weekly reporting for customer-service management, giving me directly relevant experience working with support-related text and classification workflows." Keep the existing RAG disclosure immediately afterward so the prototype is not presented as production experience.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the second paragraph, replace the broad phrase "model versioning with MLflow" with the more precise supported wording "experiment tracking and model registry with MLflow." This matches the candidate's documented experience exactly and avoids implying a broader data-versioning capability that is not evidenced in the original information.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the final paragraph, replace "contribute to systems that make support more useful for merchants and agents" with a more role-specific statement such as "contribute to systems that answer merchant questions, route support requests and help agents resolve issues efficiently." This uses the job description's terminology while remaining a truthful statement of the target contribution.
